Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Money, work & business · Town, shops & places

sale noun

selling

also sales, a sale

classical

Cic. Rosc. Am. 110: bonōrum (Lewis & Short)
Sen. Ben. 5.10.1 (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 131, 373

1vēnditiō: long e (Lewis & Short leaves it unmarked). From vēndō, contracted from vēnum dō (de Vaan 663, s.v. vēnum), as this lexicon writes it (see sell). Spanish keeps a close vowel: vendo, beside tiendo from tendō. Traupman prints vēnditiō (pp. 131, 373).

vēnditiō1, vēnditiōnis f.

noun, third declension

a selling, a sale

The act of selling; in Cicero the sale of a man’s goods (bonōrum vēnditiō, Rosc. Am. 110). For sale is vēnālis (see for sale).

Other words

  • auctiō, auctiōnis f. — a sale by auction

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 12.3; Plaut. Men. 5.9.91–94 (Lewis & Short: auctiōnem facere)

    A public sale to the highest bidder, a crier (praecō) calling the bids (Lewis & Short).

See also sell, for sale, seller, discount, price.
